chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman whose husband was afflicted such that he could never perform sexual intercourse; should she divorce him? He said: Yes, if she wishes.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a wife if her husband is permanently unable to have sexual intercourse?
ai.summary: In this ruling from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a woman whose husband suffers from permanent impotence (*al-‘Inn*) retains the unilateral right to initiate separation, emphasizing her agency in dissolving the marital bond. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for understanding *faskh* (judicial annulment) rather than just *khul'* (redemption), as the defect prevents the fulfillment of the marriage's primary purpose. It highlights the practical application of removing hardship (*darar*) from the wife when the husband is unable to perform his conjugal duties permanently.
